newsitem.title: UK: Brady debt up but activity light ahead of U.S PPI.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt up but activity light ahead of U.S PPI.

text.p: Brady bond prices were firmer on Friday in continued reaction to U.S. retail sales figures on Thursday that showed the strong pace of U.S. economic growth was beginning to subside, emerging market traders said.

They said activity remained extremely thin ahead of the release of May's U.S. producer price index (PPI) today at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. "Trading activity is quiet going into PPI but most people are still bullish," said a trader at a European investment bank here.

Another trader said there was buying in Argentina, Bulgaria and Russian instruments on Friday and that should continue as long as the inflation numbers are relatively benign because there is still a lot of cash that needs to be put to work.

Others said the market was poised to reach new highs if wholesale inflation data meets consensus forecasts, showing little sign the Federal Reserve would move to raise rates at the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on July 1 and July 2.
According to a Reuters poll, economists see a mere 0.1 percent rise in both the PPI and the core rate, which excludes the volatile food and energy segments.

"People are saying if we get decent figures today then the Fed is just going to move aside and there will be no worries in our market anymore of a rise in interest rates, and then the market is just going to go crazy," a trader at a U.S. investment bank here said.

"I think the market is in a state of mind where bullish news is being interpreted as bullish and bearish news is being ignored, so unless its a very bad number I would expect to see a positive reaction," added another trader.

The main concern in the market over the longer term is that an overabundance of supply in the emerging Eurobond market could push Brady prices lower but analysts added those fears have yet to be realised.

"The only worry down the line is that a lot of supply is coming out. Every single country you hear about is doing some five- or 10- year deal. It's a worry down the line but right now people can't get enough of it," said a market source.

Argentine pars were up one percentage point at 69-7/8 bid, Bulgarian FLRBs were 7/8 stronger at 55-3/8 bid and Russian Vneshekonombank dollar loans were 1/2 higher at 90-1/2 bid. --Diane Craft, London Newsroom 44 171 542 5110
